fact.box: bitcoin held directly, no account wrapper
fact.claim: Bitcoin fell to about US$15,480 in November 2022 as the FTX collapse unfolded, its lowest price since November 2020. On November 5, 2026, after slipping back below US$80,000, it traded around US$79,356 to US$79,600, roughly five times that low, so US$1,000 bought at the bottom would be worth about US$5,100 today and someone who sold there missed about US$4,100 of that gain. The math assumes a purchase at the exact low, which almost nobody managed, and uses US-dollar prices before fees and taxes; the result in Canadian dollars will differ a little because the exchange rate has moved. Bitcoin is still about 37% below its all-time high, and its past recoveries do not promise future ones.
